text: The glass frog keeps its heart visible through translucent skin on its underside.
Arctic terns migrate from pole to pole each year, the longest journey of any animal.
Axolotls can regrow entire limbs, including bones, nerves, and muscle tissue.
Honeybees communicate the direction and distance of flowers through a waggle dance.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue, copper-based blood instead of iron-based blood.
The axolotl's name comes from an Aztec word meaning water monster.
Wombat droppings are cube shaped, which keeps them from rolling away on slopes.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance when they gather to feed together.
Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of outer space by entering a cryptobiotic state.
The mantis shrimp punches with the speed of a bullet, shattering aquarium glass.
Bananas are berries botanically, while strawberries technically are not berries.
Lightning strikes the Earth about eight million times every single day.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on the planet, visible from orbit.
Hummingbirds can fly backwards and upside down, unique among all bird species.
Trees in a forest share nutrients and warnings through underground fungal networks.
The Sahara desert was green savanna with lakes and rivers roughly six thousand years ago.
A single teaspoon of neutron star matter would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Crows recognize individual human faces and can remember a grudge for years.
The moon is drifting away from Earth at roughly the speed your fingernails grow.
Deep sea vents support entire ecosystems that never see sunlight or rely on photosynthesis.
Squirrels plant thousands of trees each year by forgetting where they buried their nuts.
The human nose can distinguish roughly a trillion different scents, far more than once thought.
Bamboo can grow nearly a meter in a single day, the fastest growth of any plant.
Elephants are the only mammals that cannot jump, yet they can recognize themselves in mirrors.
